title: From Photonics Precision to Repeatable Evidence - Semiwiki
gist: Moh Kolb argues that silicon photonics has already proven laboratory-grade optical alignment precision, and that the real manufacturing boundary for co-packaged optics and optical I/O is repeatability: converting expert-driven one-off measurements into automated, calibrated, condition-tagged manufacturing evidence that separates device variation from test-system variation and enables yield learning.

themes.theme: Precision versus repeatability as the real bottleneck

insights.claim: Silicon photonics has already demonstrated that extremely precise optical alignment is achievable in controlled laboratory environments, so precision itself is no longer the industry's open problem.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Reframes where value accrues in photonics: away from demo-stage precision claims, toward production test infrastructure.
insights.quote: Silicon photonics has already shown that extremely precise optical alignment is possible.
insights.locator: Why Optical Probing Is Becoming a Manufacturing Boundary

insights.claim: A single successful measurement demonstrates capability while a measurement repeated thousands of times creates evidence, and only the latter supports scale.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: A test for separating photonics companies with real manufacturing readiness from those with impressive one-off demos.
insights.quote: A successful measurement once demonstrates capability.
insights.locator: A successful measurement once demonstrates capability

insights.claim: Accuracy and repeatability are distinct properties: a measurement can be correct once and still be unsuitable for manufacturing if repeat readings on the same device differ materially.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Datasheet accuracy specs are the wrong diligence metric for photonics test tools; ask for repeatability and reproducibility data.
insights.quote: A measurement can be accurate once and still be unsuitable for manufacturing.
insights.locator: Accuracy and Repeatability Are Not the Same

insights.claim: The decisive capability of a photonics test system is whether it can distinguish device variation from measurement-system variation, because without that separation observed changes cannot be attributed to product or to test.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Gauge capability rather than raw precision becomes the purchasing criterion for photonics probe platforms.
insights.locator: Can the system distinguish device variation

themes.theme: Why photonics probing is structurally harder than electrical probing

insights.claim: Photonic alignment is sensitive to very small variations in position, height, angle, polarization, wavelength and temperature, so a mechanically insignificant shift can materially change the optical measurement.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Explains why photonics test time and tool cost per device are structurally higher than electrical test, a cost line in co-packaged optics economics.
insights.quote: A shift that appears insignificant mechanically can materially change the optical measurement.
insights.locator: Photonics adds another layer of sensitivity

insights.claim: Characterizing a modulator can simultaneously require optical input and output coupling, high-speed electrical drive signals, DC bias control, RF probing, polarization management, thermal stabilization, optical-power measurement and bandwidth analysis in one setup.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: The multi-domain co-test requirement favors integrated platform vendors over point-instrument suppliers.
insights.locator: A modulator, for example, may require

insights.claim: A photonic measurement result depends on the alignment method, probe condition, fiber position, calibration state, optical path, test sequence, environmental stability and controlling software, which makes the probe platform itself part of the evidence chain rather than a passive instrument.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Elevates test equipment from a capex line item to a qualification-critical supplier with high switching costs.
insights.quote: This makes the probe platform part of the evidence chain.
insights.locator: The result depends not only on the device

insights.claim: When measured insertion loss changes, the plausible causes span device change, fiber movement, polarization drift, optical source change, calibration reference aging, temperature shift and probe contact effects, and unresolved ambiguity among them blocks manufacturing decisions.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Illustrates the diagnostic burden that drives demand for instrumented, condition-logging test systems.
insights.locator: When measured insertion loss changes, did the device change?

themes.theme: From measurement data to manufacturing evidence

insights.claim: The traditional photonics test objective of aligning the light and measuring the device must be replaced by a broader manufacturing objective: align, measure, calibrate, repeat, compare and preserve the conditions behind the result.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: A concrete checklist for evaluating whether a photonics fab or assembly partner has production-grade test discipline.
insights.quote: Align, measure, calibrate, repeat, compare, and preserve the conditions behind the result.
insights.locator: From Alignment to Evidence

insights.claim: Useful manufacturing evidence includes alignment position and search history, optical input power, polarization state, wavelength and spectral conditions, stage and chuck temperature, electrical bias and drive settings, calibration status, probe and fiber identification, measurement uncertainty, device location and wafer context, and repeated-measurement variation.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Defines the data schema photonics test platforms must emit, an integration hook for test-data-analytics vendors.
insights.locator: Useful manufacturing evidence may include

insights.claim: A coupling-loss value reported without its measurement conditions is difficult to compare against another result, whereas a calibrated repeatable value tied to its operating conditions can support yield analysis, process improvement, qualification and product release.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Condition-tagged test data is the prerequisite for photonics yield learning; vendors lacking it will lag on yield ramp.
insights.locator: A coupling-loss value without its measurement conditions

insights.claim: Repeatable probing lets engineers determine whether variation originates from lithography, etch, deposition, bonding, optical coupling, metallization, packaging or test setup, and whether a process adjustment truly improved performance or merely changed the measurement condition.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Repeatability is the gating input to the yield-learning loop that determines photonics cost curves.
insights.locator: Repeatability Enables Learning

insights.claim: Without repeatability each measurement risks becoming an isolated observation, so the causal chain runs from repeatability to comparable evidence to process learning to yield improvement.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Gives a mechanistic reason why test infrastructure investment must precede photonics margin expansion.
insights.quote: Without repeatability, each measurement risks becoming an isolated observation.
insights.locator: Without repeatability, each measurement risks

insights.claim: Manual photonics alignment can produce excellent results in development laboratories but manual expertise does not scale, because high-volume manufacturing cannot depend on one person recognizing the correct fiber angle or deciding when coupling is good enough.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Labor-intensive photonics test is a scaling ceiling; automation vendors capture the transition.
insights.quote: But manual expertise is difficult to scale.
insights.locator: Why Automation Matters

insights.claim: Automation converts tacit expert knowledge into a repeatable sequence covering device location, safe approach to the coupling region, optical power search, position and angle optimization, electrical contact verification, calibration, measurement execution, abnormal-result detection, realignment and evidence storage.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Specifies the automated-probe feature set buyers should demand, useful for comparing competing platforms.
insights.quote: Automation converts tacit expertise into a repeatable sequence.
insights.locator: Automation converts tacit expertise

insights.claim: Automation does not eliminate engineering judgment but relocates it into the design of the measurement process, so the quality of the automation itself becomes part of product quality.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Test-process software becomes a differentiator and a source of recurring value rather than a commodity wrapper around hardware.
insights.quote: The quality of the automation then becomes part of product quality.
insights.locator: This does not eliminate engineering judgment.

insights.claim: Platforms from companies such as FormFactor illustrate the transition from expert-driven optical alignment toward automated and repeatable photonics probing, though the deeper change is described as methodological rather than equipment-driven.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Names an identifiable public-market beneficiary of the photonics production-test buildout.
insights.quote: Platforms from companies such as FormFactor illustrate this transition from expert-driven optical alignment toward automated and repeatable photonics probing.
insights.locator: Platforms from companies such as FormFactor

themes.theme: Second-order implications for CPO and design flow

insights.claim: In co-packaged optics and optical I/O the product is not ready merely because the modulator, detector, coupling structure and electrical interface each work once; reproducibility after assembly, across temperature, through process variation and over expected operating life is what determines readiness.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: A skeptical lens on co-packaged optics timelines: component-level demos do not de-risk volume ramp.
insights.locator: The Hidden Boundary in CPO and Optical I/O

insights.claim: Probing strategy can influence device layout, coupler placement, pad access, fiber-array geometry, calibration structures, test time, packaging sequence and known-good-die strategy, so testability must enter the photonic design flow early rather than being treated as downstream test.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Design-for-test in photonics becomes an EDA and PDK opportunity and a differentiator among photonic IP providers.
insights.quote: Testability must therefore enter the design flow early.
insights.locator: In reality, the probing strategy can influence device layout

insights.claim: A photonic architecture that is difficult to probe, calibrate or compare is likely also difficult to manufacture economically, linking test complexity directly to unit cost.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Probe-ability becomes a screen for which photonic architectures can reach cost-competitive volume.
insights.quote: A photonic architecture that is difficult to probe, calibrate, or compare may also be difficult to manufacture economically.
insights.locator: A photonic architecture that is difficult to probe

insights.claim: Photonics probe platforms should be understood not as microscopes, stages, fibers and instruments assembled around a wafer but as infrastructure required to transform optical performance into manufacturing confidence.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: Argues for a higher strategic valuation on photonics test infrastructure than on generic laboratory instrumentation.
insights.locator: From Precision to Scale

insights.claim: The future of photonics manufacturing will be determined less by laboratory alignment precision and more by whether that precision converts into a repeatable, automatable and trusted evidence path, potentially making this one of the most important hidden realization boundaries for co-packaged optics, optical I/O and photonic integrated circuits.
insights.speaker: Moh Kolb
insights.so_what: If correct, test-and-evidence capability rather than device physics is the gating item for the photonics-for-AI thesis.
insights.locator: The future of photonics manufacturing will not be determined
